svg.text: EmbedSeek (proposed method): search several embedding spaces with a two-level bandit, then train one fixed proxy
(b) Two-level bandit chooses what to label
needed anyway: the proxy must score every row
similarity ∪ a random slice → cuts encoder cost
= the arms of the second level
Same rows, different geometry: each encoder
Embedding cost = C_proxy(N) + Σₘ s · C_m(N)
Thompson sampling: draw a score from each
encoder's Beta(wins, losses); take the largest
(top level: one arm per embedding space)
② Pick a cluster inside it
Same Thompson sampling over the chosen
③ Propose a batch of b rows from that cluster
likely positives first (LR in that encoder's space), rest random
human labels now, an LLM later: the expensive step
r = 1 if the batch contains a positive; update the
cluster and the encoder; decay old counts (δ ≈ 0.99)
repeat until B rows are labeled
Dashed arrow = shared labels (option): each labeled row also
updates its cluster in every other encoder (one label, M updates)
Warm start (option): one query-seeded batch per encoder first
Pick the score cutoff on val
Score every row in the table
one dot product per row, no LLM calls
precision · recall · F1 · AP + bootstrap CIs
Every sampler feeds this same proxy,
so a better F1 means better training rows,
Schematic only: the cluster scatters are illustrative, not real data. Steps ①–⑤ are proposed; LTS-lite (② alone, one encoder) is implemented.
